RESEARCH VERDICT
Verdict: accumulate
Risk: medium
Confidence: 0.75
Rationale: Research confirms the buy screen on H1 profit, 0.1x leverage and a raised interim; H1 FCF of £16.4m did not cover £35.7m dividends (stated H2 cash bias) and cyclical risk remains.
RiskTags: cyclical, competitive

COMPARISON EVIDENCE

EVIDENCE
- [filings/bodies/5a239384189d0666.txt] "Revenue 1,608.0 1,457.7 +10.3% +11.1% Underlying operating profit 1 117.9 102.6 +14.9% +17.1%" — H1 2026 growth supports the buy screen’s quality and earnings-momentum case.
- [filings/bodies/5a239384189d0666.txt] "The Group's free cash inflow of £16.4m (H1 2025: £14.3m) is broadly flat on the prior period." — H1 FCF is thin versus cash returns; dividend-family pass rests on full-year, not first-half, cover.
- [filings/bodies/5a239384189d0666.txt] "The operating cash conversion of 36% (H1 2025: 50%) reflects our usual H2 bias for cash generation." — Filing explanation for H1 FCF of £16.4m versus dividends paid of £35.7m (cover below 1.0× in the half).
- [filings/bodies/5a239384189d0666.txt] "Net debt to underlying EBITDA leverage, calculated excluding the impact of IFRS 16, was 0.1x (H1 2025: 0.2x)" — Balance-sheet headroom underpins the risk-family pass; adjusted_signal remains buy, in line with the raw screen.
- [filings/bodies/ch_02442580_MzUyMzYyMjA2OWFkaXF6a2N4.txt] "£175.9m -9%" — FY 2025 filing APM free cash flow; screen filing-aligned FCF is £168.0m (Yahoo annual) and screen TTM is £189.6m.
- [filings/bodies/63e24814661003ff.txt] "Inability to maintain a sustainable level of financial performance throughout the construction industry market cycle" — Principal-risk language the screen’s cyclical overlay did not flag.
- [filings/bodies/96c9f68290ff4b47.txt] "Keller has now secured c.$1bn of work in relation to the I-40 reconstruction, of which c.10% has been completed so far." — Record order book (£2.4bn) is concentrated in a multi-year US highway programme still early in delivery.
- [filings/bodies/5bdc6901f00c2a30.txt] "The Group confirms that current trading remains in line with the Board’s expectations, as announced at the interim results on 4 August 2026." — October CMD did not change the upgraded FY 2026 trajectory.

NUMBERS
- Revenue | 1,608.0 | H1 2026 | [filings/bodies/5a239384189d0666.txt]
- Underlying operating profit | 117.9 | H1 2026 | [filings/bodies/5a239384189d0666.txt]
- Free cash flow | 16.4 | H1 2026 | [filings/bodies/5a239384189d0666.txt]
- Dividends paid to shareholders | (35.7) | H1 2026 | [filings/bodies/5a239384189d0666.txt]
- Free cash flow | £175.9m | FY 2025 | [filings/bodies/ch_02442580_MzUyMzYyMjA2OWFkaXF6a2N4.txt]
- filing_aligned free_cashflow | 168000000.0 | FY 2025 (Yahoo annual; screen uses this) | [screening_snapshot.json]

THESIS BREAKS
- Full-year free cash flow covering cash dividends below 1.0×, or an announced interim dividend cut, reversing the dividend-family pass (H1 2026 FCF of £16.4m already did not cover £35.7m dividends paid).
- Board withdrawal of the July/August FY 2026 upgrade, or a sharp contraction in the order book from the c.£2.4bn I-40-inflated level, consistent with a construction-market downturn.
- Material losses, disputes or impairments on the I-40 programme (c.$1bn secured; c.10% complete; three to four years remaining) that reverse North America margins.
- Net debt/EBITDA moving above the 3.0× covenant (0.1× at 30 June 2026), or a going-concern qualification.
